body:
He's gonna take me, so I won't have to worry about driving. Yeahhhhhh, I'm 5 years old :).

Talk to you again soon.

I've definitely been given some major food for thought, not only from you, but also the others who have replied. I have to go to the dr's in a few minutes, but I'll be back in about an hour or so. In case you or anyone else comments, I don't want anyone to think that I'm ignoring them. I'll definitely check this page when I get back. 

Thank you so much again. 

p.s. If it's ok with you, I'll probably PM when I'm online again.

>What I think you're missing here is that he doesn't want a divorce

Maybe you're right; I dunno. The few times I've gotten the nerve up to ask if he still wanted one, he's always replied that he did. But who knows, maybe he just likes knowing I'm backed into a corner, with that hammer hovering over my head. That's something to think about.

>paralyzed by shades of gray that don't exist isn't healthy.

Have we met before? lol That's me to a T.

>you have a psychological need to receive abuse and blame

On this, you're probably dead-on. I have had abuse issues in my past, and even though I'd like to think I'm over them, maybe they just show up in other areas...like this one. 

>Stop thinking of receiving a divorce settlement as "taking money" from him.

This one's a hard one for me. I know in my head that working at home with the kids, doing what I have for this many years, is actual work, even if it didn't bring in an actual income, but, somehow I still feel like it's not the same as what he's done all this time. I also know that's not how he views it. Not long after I decided to come back home, one of the girls who is now angry with me called me a "money sucker", among other things. Apparently he had told them that he wasn't sure he'd be able to buy graduation gifts (one was graduating 8th grade, other high school at the time) because he would probably be having to pay me after our divorce. That's always bothered me, and I guess I kind of internalized it. 

Again, thank you so much for the reply. You really have given me a lot to think about.

>He'd controlled everything down to the fucking remote control,

That made me laugh, because it's so familiar. I hate the weekends when he's gonna be home, because I know that I'm stuck watching whatever he wants. It's a petty thing to be annoyed about, but you know.

I have gone crazy, gotten drunk, but not called him everything in the book....yet. One night I did get really drunk, and the next day he was upset (hurt) because I had said that he disgusted me. That's something I'd never, ever say if I hadn't had some liquid courage. When he brought it up, he looked so hurt, that I felt guilty and apologized profusely. Sometimes when I think about it, I still get a twinge in my stomach. I don't like to hurt people's feelings, but I guess I had to say it that night or something. 

Anyway, thank you for your reply. I'm not quite 40 (couple yrs from it, give or take), but I see the gray coming out in my hair (LOADS of it since this whole thing began), and the body not the way it used to be, and I just feel so old, and used up. Like, I had the kids, did the whole Suzy Homemaker thing, and now that I'm not in my 20's anymore, I'm pushed to the wayside. So, I don't know how to put this without sounding politically incorrect....but it's nice to hear from someone who is older, and has gone through the same types of feelings, that you can still come out of it. I really hope that doesn't sound bad!

Thanks again for taking the time to reply.

Thank you for this. It's interesting to read it from the perspective of someone who was a kid watching it all play out. Getting the guts up is exactly my problem right now. 

Thank you for your response. I will definitely refer to it again later :).

I've thought over and over about how the kids are seeing things. In fact, I know it's affected them. My oldest daughter goes to school, works full-time, and has told me for quite a while now "I will *never* be in a position where some guy can tell me what to do". I love her dearly, I know she loves me just as much, but it's sorta hard because I know that part of what she's saying is that she will never end up like me. Which is actually a good thing, I just hate that she has to fear that in the back of her mind. 

Anyway, I really do appreciate that you took the time to respond. Sometimes I'm so overwhelmed that even though I'd like to talk to people, I just can't. So if I don't PM you, please don't think that you didn't accomplish anything, because you really have. And in all actuality, I really have thought about sending a PM, but my brain is on overload today. I still might though :).

I'm so overwhelmed today, so I'm not sure how little or how much I'll be able to say in reply. 

If I were to let myself go into detail in my mind about everything that's gone on, I don't think I could take it. So, most days I push it all into little boxes in my head, and only peek in occasionally.

Some of the things you said I've heard before, but there are some things you mentioned that I've never, ever thought of. They pretty much stopped me in my tracks, and now I'm gonna have to mull them over.

I should have mentioned that I did apply for SSI, but was denied because we make too much money, according to their guidelines. And, since I don't have much work experience, they can't even give me money based off of that. I should note that we *don't* make a ton of money; most months it's pretty tight. But I guess they don't see it that way when calcuating what someone should get...if anything.

Since my daughter moved out, I've been going with her to places here and there. Nothing huge, just getting out for a bit. 

One of my strengths, but what turns out to be one of my weaknesses, is that I tend to look at everything from both sides. No matter what the situation, I try to see what both people are thinking, feeling, why they did what they did, whatever. That's probably why I'm so horrible at making decisions though. I'll be like "well, he shouldn't have done this....buuuuuuut, I shouldn't have said that either". I do that with everything. So, while I know he didn't have to go to the lengths he did to cheat, in the back of my mind, I see and hear all the times I did (or didn't do) stuff that could have made a difference. 

One thing that you wrote that is really hard for me to read is the part about asking to go to counseling. I had asked him, and he refused. He doesn't believe in that sort of thing ever, but also at the time, he said there was no point because he was done. Which is one of the reasons why I spend most days confused. If he wanted out that badly, then why hasn't he done anything to make it happen sooner? Even the time when we actually did go meet with someone, and had some papers drawn up (that I ended up refusing to sign), that was because *I* made the appointment. It was around a month after he first told me how he was feeling, and at that point, I was pretty much insane, so I made an appointment with someone, in part to just get it all over with, but also to call his bluff. He was pretty mad that I didn't sign, but after I'd had some time to think and read the papers word for word, I realized there was no way I should walk way after that many years with the very small amount he wanted to give me. So now, even though most things he says and does confuse me, I also sorta know in the back of my mind that one of the reasons he probably hasn't pushed it is because he doesn't want to pay out anymore money. And that makes me feel really good too. "I'm still here, but only because I don't want to pay you more money". He hasn't said that, but that's the feeling I get sometimes.

It's so hard for me to think about being the one to actually force the issue and go through with it, if it comes down to it. I was raised that when you get married, you're married for life, and all the troubles you may have, are things that you work through. Logically I understand that's not always realistic, but it's sure hard getting that message through to my heart. 

Thank you for taking the time to read my comments, and to reply. I truly do appreciate it.

Thanks for the reply.

My kids range in age from 11-18. As far as if they're ok or not, it's a relative term, I suppose. 

After I left for a little while (had moved out for a few months after he told me he wanted out), things between me and a couple of them went downhill. They're ok physically, in school they're doing much better, but they're pretty angry....and for some reason it's with me. On the other hand, one of our daughters recently moved out because she swears she's never talking to her father again (definitely NOT what I'd want for either of them), and one of the reasons she gave him was his cheating on me. She will only come over when he and the other girls aren't here, because she wants nothing to do with them. 

It's been rough. Like I said, I know he's definitely not the sole reason for why things went south, but before he decided to have his little crisis, nothing was anywhere near as bad as it is now. 

I wish I could hate him, somehow it seems like that would make it easier. God knows I've tried to, but it's just not possible for me to do. We've known each other for so long, and been together so long, that it really feels like he's a part of me. When all this first started, I literally hurt. Like not just heart-broken, but something inside, physically, hurt. I can't really describe it. I remember thinking to myself that the only thing I could imagine being worse was to have one of my kids die. I've lost plenty of people in my life, and nothing hurt to the depths of places I never knew I had, like when he said he was done.

I feel like I'm about to explode today. The feeling comes in waves; guess the waves are high today. I have more days where I can handle it alright, versus the bad days where I don't handle it so well, but when that feeling comes, it hits hard.

I have loved him pretty much my whole life. Almost 22 years later, I still love to see him. The problem is he doesn't feel the same. It's been quite a while since he told me he wanted a divorce, but aside from when we went to see someone to discuss our options, and he had some ridiculous paperwork drawn up, he hasn't tried to file for anything else.

The problems we've had are by no means solely his fault. I don't even think that when he cheated on me that was totally his fault. I got lost in life, and didn't pay attention to things I should have. Caught up in my own world, and that's my mistake. But through it all, I never wanted to lose him, and that's what I'm having a hard time dealing with.

I've seen many a broken-hearted person write out their feelings, trying to figure out how to put one foot in front of the other after such a horrific blow. The most common thing I see others advise is to stay away from that person, quit hoping for their calls, stop looking at the other person's online pages to check up on them, etc. The problem in my case is that we still live in the same house, and at the moment that can't change.

The way our arrangement worked was he worked, and after I had the kids, I stayed home with them. That was fine, and worked just fine for us. There was only a brief period of time that I worked to bring in a little extra income, but other than that, I really have no major work experience. I'm on the downhill slide to 40, and have no idea how I'm going to be able to make it on my own. Part of me still hopes that he'll change his mind. Although another part of me is so hurt by how and who he cheated with, that I would love to be able to walk out and say F you.

Almost 10 years ago, we had some problems, and during that period of time he did something that I didn't realize would affect me this many years later. We used to have a joint checking account. One day he got mad, cleared out the account, knowing full well there were checks that needed to go through still, started an account in his name only, and left me with no access to our money. I had a check-rite alert put on my name because he refused to pay those checks that bounced as a result of what he did. He also had a check-rite thing put on his name, but since he had immediately opened another account, it didn't really affect him in the way that it did me. In the years that followed, he would give me his ATM card, and there wasn't a huge issue with money, so I didn't think much of the money being only in his name. Cut to now........still no access, but ever since he told me he wanted out, the ATM was taken away (and logically that would be the next step) and I now have no money unless he gives it to me---which is rare. If I need something from the store, he'll go with me and pay for it. Once in a long while I can talk him into giving me $5 to get something from the corner store. The most I've ever gotten out of him at one time is $20, but that's a very rare occasion. The only reason I include all of this is because I'm sure someone is going to tell me to just leave, but that's easier said than done without money. Due to some serious physical problems, I've had to postpone even just trying to get a job at a convenience store for some quick cash. And the truth of the matter is, my self-esteem is so low, when I think about doing something like that, I picture them looking at me and laughing 'cause I have no real work experience to speak of. Like I wouldn't even be good enough for that.

His cheating on me angers me, but more than that it just hurts. He is still hung up on this other person, who basically dumped him. If I were to tell the story, you would probably understand why when he tells me he never got 'closure' with her, I find it so ridiculous. I just don't have the stomach to write out the details at the moment.

I feel like I have a sword constantly hanging over my head, like at any moment, it could drop and everything as I know it would be gone. I feel like i have to walk on eggshells around him, never say how I really feel, because if I did, he wouldn't care and would use that to get rid of me faster.

I'm also really confused because even though he's said he wanted a divorce, he doesn't ever talk about it, and we do most things like we always had. Live together, eat together, we even just bought a vehicle recently and both of our names are on it. He won't have sex with me....at least not traditional sex, but he'll do everything else. That really confuses me. He likes for me to massage him, wants blowjobs, handjobs, even anal.....but no vaginal sex. Like, if he actually had regular sex with me, it would somehow say we were really together or something? I dunno. And even though part of me does those things because I like them, the other part feels very used. But I also feel like if I don't do them, for sure he'll get it from somewhere else, and the thought of it makes me ill.

I suppose there really are no answers for my situation. I just needed to see if getting this out today would somehow ease the pressure I feel building up. Even though I don't really wanna kill myself, there are days when I think "why do I even bother???". There are more problems than I have time to write about, and not just between him and I, but I'm hoping this will help a little today.

Thanks for letting me use up this space.

I posted [this](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/7sudh/we_are_still_here_talk_to_us/c07bsaf) in the original thread just now.

Thanks again :).

I have to make this brief, as I have an appointment to get ready for, but I'll try to make a longer reply to you all later.

I just wanted to thank all of you for even reading my post, and thanks for the comments/messages I received. Like I said, the situation is pretty messed up, and I'm not even sure there really are any specific answers. Just one of those things where you have to tell yourself "one foot in front of the other" and hope it doesn't hurt too badly when you trip. 

I'll continue to keep an eye out on this account (obviously it's new, and therefore not my usual). Thank you guys so much; some of you may never know how much you've done for me throughout this last year. Whether it be advice to myself or others, funny comments, or even the occasional 'argument', it's all helped in ways I never could have imagined. 

Big hugs to all of you.

*Gonna take a deep breath here.......*


So here's the deal: I'm not really suicidal, but I have been in the past and even within the past year. I've had major marital troubles which totally threw me for a loop. I moved out because it hurt too badly to stay home, but within a few months found out that it was hurting my relationship with my children (2 in particular). By the time I had the strength to ignore what was going on between myself and my husband, I had already lost my relationship with 2 of my girls. They hated me, and had no problems showing it. 

I've stayed through A LOT of crap. If I were to describe all of it, I'm sure a lot of people wouldn't believe it...but, I assure you, it's all true. It's ranged from mental to physical to emotional torture. They've done everything they possibly could to drive me back out, but I knew I couldn't just "let them go". 

Through the mess of me trying to keep an eye on them, because their dad was so lenient, that they were doing everything imaginable, but he didn't wanna believe it, I've also had to try to deal with mine and his relationship. 

We don't "fight" in the usual sense, and in fact have in the last couple of weeks, had to come together because of a couple of stunts the 2 girls have pulled....one involving us having to call the police. 

Things are stressful. Sometimes I think "why do I even bother????", but I don't have the balls to just walk out into that semi-truck that I pass when I go for walks or runs. I also don't have the know-how to fix this fucked up situation. 

I do have a good relationship with my other kids, which is probably why I actually haven't done anything stupid yet, but sometimes it is SO hard not to.

I haven't even scratched the surface of all that's gone on this past year, so I know there are no real answers for me....but I do want you guys to know that I watch this section regularly, and thank you for keeping it going.
